renders.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Wood vs. the lunch line. Truffaut to a lunch lady. Corn. Panel 1: a gaunt teenage boy in an oversized wool overcoat leaning over a cafeteria tray toward a bored lunch lady with a ladle, serving line with a sneeze guard and a heat lamp, fluorescent glare, 1990s high school cafeteria. Wood says "Do you ever consider that this room is the only place in Small Wood where three hundred people voluntarily sit in the same direction?". Panel 2: close two-shot across a cafeteria counter, a lunch lady with a raised ladle giving a flat stare to a gaunt teenage boy in an overcoat, steam rising. Lunch Lady says "Corn or peas.". Panel 3: a teenage boy in a wool overcoat holding a cafeteria tray turns to face the viewer declaiming, the lunch line moving on behind him, heavy black shadows. Wood says "Truffaut said the film of tomorrow will be an act of love. I said corn.". Panel 4: wide shot of a long empty cafeteria table, a teenage boy in an overcoat alone at the near end with a plate of corn, far in the background a boy in a backwards cap drawing on a napkin and a girl with headphones reading, rain on tall windows, lots of empty table. No dialogue in this panel. In the bottom right margin, tiny hand-lettered signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes.
